_note: Short original bios, written in our own words from public sources. The build adds each one only when the database has no bio, so an admin edit always wins. Keys are person ids.
prakash-raj: Actor, director, producer and politician who works across Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Hindi and English films. Best known as one of Indian cinema's most versatile character actors and screen villains, he has won five National Film Awards.
kamal-haasan: Actor, filmmaker and politician who works mainly in Tamil cinema, and a Rajya Sabha member for Tamil Nadu. Beginning as a child actor, he has also written, directed, produced and sung for films over six decades, and is known for taking on many roles in a single film.
amitabh-bachchan: One of the most celebrated actors in the history of Hindi cinema, with more than 200 films since 1969. Famous as the 'Angry Young Man' of the 1970s, he has also worked as a playback singer, producer and long-running quiz show host.
rajinikanth: Born Shivaji Rao Gaikwad, he is a Tamil cinema superstar with a career of more than five decades and around 170 films in several languages, celebrated for his unmistakable style and mass appeal.
mohanlal: Malayalam cinema's most prolific star, with more than 400 films over four decades, along with roles in Tamil, Hindi, Telugu and Kannada films. He is also a producer, playback singer and director.
akshay-kumar: Born Akshay Hari Om Bhatia, he is a Hindi film star and producer known as 'Khiladi Kumar' for his action roles, and later for comedies and socially themed dramas. He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2009.
salman-khan: Hindi film star, producer and television host whose career spans more than three decades and over 80 films, and one of Indian cinema's biggest box-office draws.
nagarjuna: Telugu film star and producer, son of the legendary Akkineni Nageswara Rao, known for films ranging from romantic hits and action dramas to devotional epics, and for hosting television.
shah-rukh-khan: Known as SRK and the 'Baadshah of Bollywood', he has appeared in more than 90 Hindi films and is one of the most famous film stars in the world. He also produces films through his company Red Chillies Entertainment.
tamannaah: Tamannaah Bhatia is an actress who works mainly in Tamil, Telugu and Hindi films and has appeared in close to 90 films, establishing herself as a leading star of South Indian cinema.
ajay-devgn: Born Vishal Veeru Devgan, he is a Hindi film actor, director and producer with more than 100 films, known for action, intense dramas and comedy franchises. He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016.
priyanka-chopra: Actress, producer and singer who won Miss World in 2000 and became one of Hindi cinema's top stars before building a career in Hollywood film and television. She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016.
nayanthara: Actress and producer known for her work in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam films. Often called 'Lady Superstar', she has appeared in more than 75 films over two decades.
sanjay-dutt: Hindi film actor and producer with more than 135 films, often playing flawed heroes and, later in his career, formidable villains. He has also appeared in Telugu, Kannada and Tamil films.
aamir-khan: Hindi film actor, filmmaker and television host known in the media as 'Mr. Perfectionist' for his choice of roles. His films include some of the most successful Indian films of all time.
dhanush: Born Venkatesh Prabhu Kasthuri Raja, he is a Tamil actor, director, lyricist and singer who has also worked in Hindi and Telugu films, and a winner of several National Film Awards.
samantha-ruth-prabhu: Actress who works mainly in Tamil and Telugu films and is one of South India's leading stars, known for both commercial hits and performance-driven roles.
abhishek-bachchan: Hindi film actor and producer, son of Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan, known for films ranging from comedies and crime dramas to character studies.
aishwarya-rai: Aishwarya Rai Bachchan won Miss World in 1994 and became one of the best-known Indian actresses, working mainly in Hindi and Tamil films.
sridevi: Sridevi Kapoor was often called the first female superstar of Indian cinema. Starting as a child actress, she worked in Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, Malayalam and Kannada films over five decades.
priyadarshan: Director and screenwriter who has made more than 90 films since 1982, mostly in Malayalam and Hindi, and is best known for comedies and for remaking Malayalam hits in Hindi.
sunny-deol: Born Ajay Singh Deol, he is a Hindi film actor, filmmaker and former politician with more than 100 films, famous for intense, angry action heroes. He is the son of Dharmendra.
deepika-padukone: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films and is one of India's highest-paid stars. The daughter of badminton champion Prakash Padukone, she was named among Time's 100 most influential people in 2018.
hrithik-roshan: Hindi film actor and producer, son of filmmaker Rakesh Roshan, known for his dancing and for playing India's best-known film superhero, Krrish.
tovino-thomas: Malayalam actor and producer and one of the leading stars of his generation, who made his debut in 2012 and played the superhero Minnal Murali.
suriya: Born Saravanan Sivakumar, he is a Tamil film actor and producer, the son of actor Sivakumar, known for both mass entertainers and acclaimed dramas such as Soorarai Pottru and Jai Bhim.
mahesh-babu: Telugu film star, producer and philanthropist, son of the actor Krishna. Called 'Superstar' by fans and the media, he is one of the highest-paid actors in Indian cinema.
k-balachander: Playwright, director, producer and screenwriter who worked mainly in Tamil cinema and was known for bold, unconventional subjects and strong women characters. He launched the careers of Rajinikanth and Kamal Haasan among many others.
s-p-muthuraman: Tamil film director who made 72 films and was one of the most successful commercial directors in Tamil cinema, especially through his long partnership with Rajinikanth.
kareena-kapoor-khan: Actress from the Kapoor film family who has been a leading star of Hindi cinema since 2000, in roles ranging from romantic comedies to crime dramas.
trisha: Trisha Krishnan is an actress who works mainly in Tamil and Telugu films and has been a leading star of South Indian cinema for more than two decades.
akshaye-khanna: Hindi film actor, son of the actor Vinod Khanna, widely praised for his versatility in films from Dil Chahta Hai to Drishyam 2.
g-v-prakash-kumar: Music composer, actor and producer who works mainly in Tamil cinema. A child singer in the 1990s and nephew of A. R. Rahman, he made his debut as a composer with Veyil and later began acting in lead roles.
rashmika-mandanna: Actress who works mainly in Telugu and Hindi films, as well as Kannada and Tamil, and is known for leading roles in big-budget hits such as Pushpa and Animal.
alia-bhatt: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films, daughter of filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt, known for playing women in difficult circumstances, and a National Film Award winner for Gangubai Kathiawadi.
juhi-chawla: Hindi film actress who was one of the leading stars of the late 1980s and 1990s, known for her comic timing, and later a producer and businesswoman.
raveena-tandon: Hindi film actress who was one of the leading stars of the 1990s, later also known for acclaimed dramatic roles. She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2023.
manisha-koirala: Nepalese actress who works in Indian cinema, mainly in Hindi and Tamil films, and is the granddaughter of former Nepalese Prime Minister B. P. Koirala.
saif-ali-khan: Hindi film actor and producer, son of actress Sharmila Tagore and cricketer Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi, known for roles ranging from romantic comedies to dark, intense characters.
tabu: Tabassum Fatima Hashmi, known as Tabu, is an actress who works mainly in Hindi films, as well as Telugu and Tamil, and is acclaimed for performances in films such as Maachis, Chandni Bar and Andhadhun.
anil-kapoor: Hindi film actor and producer who has appeared in more than 100 films over four decades, as well as in Indian television and international productions.
arshad-warsi: Hindi film actor best known as Circuit in the Munna Bhai films and as the lawyer Jolly in Jolly LLB, who worked as an assistant director and choreographer before acting.
ayushmann-khurrana: Hindi film actor and singer known for playing ordinary men battling social norms in films such as Vicky Donor, Badhaai Ho and Andhadhun.
katrina-kaif: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films and has starred in many of the industry's biggest hits, including the Tiger spy franchise.
ramya-krishnan: Actress who has worked in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada and Hindi films over four decades, famous for playing Sivagami in Baahubali and Neelambari in Padayappa.
karisma-kapoor: Hindi film actress from the Kapoor family who was one of the top stars of the 1990s, in hits such as Raja Hindustani and Dil To Pagal Hai.
prabhu-deva: Dancer, choreographer, actor and director, known as the 'Indian Michael Jackson', who has worked in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Hindi films and directed hits such as Pokkiri and Wanted.
preity-zinta: Hindi film actress and entrepreneur who was a leading star of the late 1990s and 2000s, and co-owns the Punjab Kings cricket team.
ranbir-kapoor: Hindi film actor from the Kapoor family, son of Rishi Kapoor and Neetu Singh, known for films such as Barfi!, Rockstar, Sanju and Animal.
bobby-deol: Hindi film actor, son of Dharmendra, who was a romantic and action lead in the 1990s and found new success playing villains in Animal and other recent films.
jackie-shroff: Hindi film actor who rose to stardom with Hero in 1983 and has appeared in more than 200 films across several Indian languages.
ram-gopal-varma: Director, writer and producer who works in Telugu and Hindi cinema, known for gritty gangster and horror films such as Shiva, Satya, Company and Sarkar.
rani-mukerji: Hindi film actress known for films such as Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, Black, Hichki and Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway.
kajol: Kajol Devgan is a Hindi film actress famous for romantic classics with Shah Rukh Khan, such as Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge. She was awarded the Padma Shri in 2011.
paresh-rawal: Actor and producer with more than 240 films, mostly in Hindi, celebrated for comedy in films such as Hera Pheri and for serious roles such as Sardar.
rekha: Bhanurekha Ganesan, known as Rekha, is a Hindi film actress who has starred in more than 200 films and is considered one of the finest actresses in Indian cinema.
meena: Meena Sagar is an actress who began as a child artist and became a leading star in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam films, known for Muthu, Drishyam and many family dramas.
ravi-teja: Born Bhupatiraju Ravi Shankar, he is a Telugu film actor and producer known for his energy and comic timing, nicknamed 'Mass Maharaja'.
riteish-deshmukh: Actor, filmmaker and television presenter who works in Hindi and Marathi films, known for comedy franchises and for directing the Marathi hit Ved.
hema-malini: Actress, director, producer and politician known as the 'Dream Girl' of Hindi cinema, and a Lok Sabha member from Mathura since 2014.
john-abraham: Hindi film actor and producer who started as a model and has made his name in action films and patriotic thrillers, and as producer of Vicky Donor.
madhuri-dixit: Hindi film actress and dancer who became one of the biggest stars of the late 1980s and 1990s, in films such as Tezaab, Hum Aapke Hain Koun and Devdas.
shobana: Actress and Bharatanatyam dancer who has worked mainly in Malayalam cinema, as well as Tamil, Telugu and Hindi, and won National Film Awards for Manichitrathazhu and Mitr, My Friend.
shriya-saran: Actress who works in Tamil, Telugu and Hindi films, best known for Sivaji: The Boss and the Drishyam films.
anushka-shetty: Born Sweety Shetty, she is an actress known for Telugu and Tamil films, especially Arundhati, Baahubali and Bhaagamathie.
david-dhawan: Hindi film director who made 46 films, most of them comedies, including his many hits with Govinda such as Coolie No. 1 and Hero No. 1.
k-s-ravikumar: Tamil film director, screenwriter and actor, one of the most commercially successful directors of Indian cinema, known for Muthu, Padayappa and Avvai Shanmugi.
mani-ratnam: Director, producer and screenwriter who works mainly in Tamil cinema, known for Nayakan, Roja, Bombay and the two-part Ponniyin Selvan.
r-madhavan: Ranganathan Madhavan is an actor, writer, producer and director who works mainly in Tamil and Hindi films, known for Alaipayuthey, 3 Idiots and Rocketry: The Nambi Effect.
rishi-kapoor: Hindi film actor from the Kapoor family, son of Raj Kapoor, who became a romantic star with Bobby in 1973 and later won acclaim for character roles such as in Kapoor & Sons.
soundarya: Actress who worked mainly in Telugu cinema, as well as Kannada, Tamil, Hindi and Malayalam films, and is remembered as one of the finest actresses in Telugu film history.
sripriya: Actress, director and politician who appeared in more than 300 films across Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Hindi, and directed the Tamil film Drushyam.
asin: Asin Thottumkal is a former actress who worked in Tamil, Hindi and Telugu films, best known for Ghajini, Pokkiri and Sivakasi.
dharmendra: Hindi film actor, producer and politician known as the 'He-Man' of Bollywood, and one of the most successful stars in Indian cinema, with classics such as Sholay and Chupke Chupke. He was the father of Sunny Deol and Bobby Deol.
pankaj-tripathi: Actor who works mainly in Hindi films and series. After training at the National School of Drama, he became widely known through Gangs of Wasseypur, Mirzapur and Mimi.
prithviraj-sukumaran: Malayalam actor, producer, director and singer with more than 100 films, who directed Lucifer and its sequel L2: Empuraan.
revathi: Actress, director and dancer known for her work in Tamil and Malayalam cinema, as well as Telugu, Hindi and Kannada films, and the director of Mitr, My Friend and Salaam Venky.
simran: Actress who works mainly in Tamil and Telugu films and was one of the leading stars of the late 1990s and 2000s.
sree-vishnu: Telugu film actor who broke through with Prema Ishq Kaadhal and is known for films such as Brochevarevarura and Samajavaragamana.
suniel-shetty: Hindi film actor, producer and entrepreneur, nicknamed 'Anna', who has appeared in more than 100 films since the 1990s in action and comedy roles.
suraj-venjaramoodu: Malayalam actor and comedian with more than 250 films, who moved from comedy to acclaimed dramatic roles and won a National Film Award.
urvashi: Actress, screenwriter and producer who has worked mainly in Malayalam and Tamil cinema for more than four decades.
venkatesh: Daggubati Venkatesh is a Telugu film actor and producer whose career spans more than five decades, known for family dramas and comedies.
vijay: C. Joseph Vijay was a leading Tamil film star for three decades before entering politics. He founded the party Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam and became Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu in May 2026.
yash: Kannada film actor and producer known as 'Rocking Star', who became a pan-Indian star with the KGF films.
yogi-babu: Tamil actor and comedian who rose from minor roles to become one of the most popular comedians in Tamil cinema, and also plays leads in films such as Mandela.
bipasha-basu: Hindi film actress who was one of the leading stars of the 2000s, especially in thrillers and horror films such as Raaz.
chiranjeevi: Born Konidela Chiranjeevi and known as 'Megastar', he is one of the most successful actors in the history of Telugu cinema, celebrated for his dancing and action, and a former politician.
jaya-prada: Actress and politician who starred in Telugu and Hindi films from the 1970s to the 1990s, and later served in Parliament.
krishna-vamsi: Telugu film director, screenwriter and producer whose films include Sindhooram, Murari and Khadgam.
naseeruddin-shah: Actor who works mainly in Hindi films and is a leading figure of India's parallel cinema movement, with films from Sparsh and Ardh Satya to A Wednesday and international productions.
puri-jagannadh: Telugu film director and screenwriter who debuted with Badri in 2000 and is known for Pokiri, Businessman and iSmart Shankar.
radhika-sarathkumar: Radikaa Sarathkumar is an actress, producer and director working mainly in Tamil and Telugu films and television.
shilpa-shetty: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films, debuting with Baazigar, and is also known as a television judge and fitness entrepreneur.
bhumika-chawla: Actress known mainly for Telugu films such as Kushi and Okkadu, as well as Hindi films including Tere Naam.
i-v-sasi: Director who made more than 110 films, mostly in Malayalam, and was one of the most influential filmmakers in Malayalam cinema.
jyothika: Jyothika Saravanan is an actress and producer who works mainly in Tamil and Hindi films, known for Kushi, Chandramukhi and 36 Vayadhinile.
n-t-rama-rao-jr: Known as NTR Jr., he is a Telugu film star and grandson of the legendary N. T. Rama Rao, internationally known for RRR.
sathyan-anthikad: Malayalam film director, screenwriter and lyricist who has made more than 50 films over five decades, known for warm family dramas set in rural Kerala.
sonakshi-sinha: Actress who works in Hindi films and series, daughter of actor-politician Shatrughan Sinha, who debuted opposite Salman Khan in Dabangg.
brahmanandam: Telugu comic actor whose screen career runs past a thousand films, a body of work recognised by Guinness World Records as the most screen credits for a living actor. A fixture of Telugu blockbusters for decades, he still turns up in big recent releases such as Kalki 2898 AD and Game Changer.
anupam-kher: Actor, director and producer who works mainly in Hindi cinema, with more than 540 films across a career of over four decades. He has won two National Film Awards and eight Filmfare Awards, and his recent films include Emergency and The Bengal Files.
mammootty: Malayalam cinema's long-reigning leading man, an actor and producer with more than 400 films over five decades, most of them in lead roles. Alongside Malayalam he has worked in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Hindi and English, and he is still headlining films such as Abraham Ozler.
irrfan-khan: Actor (1967–2020) celebrated for quiet, naturalistic performances in Hindi cinema and in British and American films. Across a career of more than 30 years he won a National Film Award among many honours; his later Hindi work includes Hindi Medium and Blackmail.
boman-irani: Actor and comedian who came to films relatively late and went on to more than 100 roles, mostly in Hindi. Also a producer, director, voice artist and photographer, he has won a Filmfare Award and two IIFA Awards.
om-puri: Actor (1950–2017) whose four-decade career took him from a railway town in Punjab to two National Film Awards. Best known for Hindi films, he also worked in English, Punjabi, Kannada, Telugu and Malayalam cinema, and in British productions.
shahid-kapoor: Hindi film actor who first made his name in romantic roles and has since moved into action films and thrillers. One of the industry's highest-paid stars, he has appeared on Forbes India's Celebrity 100 list every year since 2012.
sunil-shetty: Actor, producer, television host and entrepreneur known for Hindi films, where fans call him Anna. Since the 1990s he has appeared in more than 100 films, in both leading and supporting action and comedy roles.
vikram: Tamil actor and playback singer known for transforming himself physically for his roles. He is among the most decorated actors in Indian cinema, with a National Film Award and nine Filmfare Awards South, and he played Aditha Karikalan in Ponniyin Selvan.
nithya-menen: Actress and singer who works across Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada films and is known for choosing performance-driven roles. Her recent films include Idli Kadai.
govinda: Actor turned politician who has appeared in more than 160 Hindi films. A leading star of the late 1980s, 1990s and early 2000s, he is remembered for his comic timing, dancing and slapstick energy, especially in his comedies with director David Dhawan.
kangana-ranaut: Actress, filmmaker and politician, elected to the Lok Sabha from Mandi in 2024. Known for strong-willed, unconventional heroines in women-led Hindi films, she has won four National Film Awards, and she directed and starred in Emergency.
prabhas: Telugu star who became a pan-Indian name with the Baahubali films. One of the highest-paid actors in India, he has appeared on Forbes India's Celebrity 100 list since 2015, and his recent films include Kalki 2898 AD and The Raja Saab.
a-sreekar-prasad: Film editor who has cut more than 600 films in over 35 years, across Hindi, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and Assamese cinema. He has won nine National Film Awards, seven of them for editing, and his recent work includes Devara: Part 1 and Indian 2.
ileana-d-cruz: Actress who works mainly in Telugu and Hindi films and holds Portuguese citizenship. She has won a Filmfare Award and a Filmfare Award South, and her Hindi films include Raid and The Big Bull.
dr-puneeth-rajkumar: Kannada actor, singer and producer (1975–2021), the son of matinee idol Dr. Rajkumar, affectionately known to fans as Appu. He won a National Film Award as a child actor for Bettada Hoovu before becoming one of Kannada cinema's biggest stars; his later films include Yuvarathnaa.
fahadh-faasil: Actor and producer working mainly in Malayalam and Tamil films, widely regarded as one of the finest actors in Indian cinema for his varied, understated performances. He is among the most popular and highest-paid stars in Malayalam cinema.
trisha-krishnan: Actress who has been a leading lady in Tamil and Telugu cinema for more than two decades, making her one of the most enduring and highest-paid actresses in the country. She played Kundavai in Ponniyin Selvan.
kota-srinivasa-rao: Actor and politician (1942–2025) known above all for Telugu cinema and theatre, where he played memorable villains and character roles. He also worked in Tamil, Hindi, Kannada and Malayalam films.
nawazuddin-siddiqui: Hindi film actor who rose from small parts to leading roles on the strength of intense, unglamorous performances. He has won a National Film Award, an IIFA Award and two Filmfare Awards, and was nominated for an International Emmy.
pritam-chakraborty: National Film Award-winning composer who studied sound engineering at FTII and worked on ad jingles and TV themes before scoring films. He is one of Hindi cinema's most in-demand music directors, with recent work including Brahmastra: Part One and Tiger 3.
allu-arjun: Telugu star known for his dancing and screen presence, whose Pushpa films made him a pan-Indian name. One of the highest-paid actors in Indian cinema, he has appeared on Forbes India's Celebrity 100 list since 2014.
vijay-sethupathi: Actor and producer who works mostly in Tamil films and occasionally in Telugu and Hindi, moving easily between heroes, villains and character parts. One of the highest-paid actors in India, he has won a National Film Award among other honours.
sneha: Actress who works mainly in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam films, in both lead and supporting roles. She has won two Tamil Nadu State Film Awards and a Filmfare Award.
vidya-balan: Hindi film actress credited with changing how women are written on screen through a run of women-led hits. She has won a National Film Award and several Filmfare Awards.
ajith-kumar: Tamil star, fondly called Thala by fans, who has headlined more than 60 films; he is also a motor-racing driver. His awards include three Filmfare Awards South and three Tamil Nadu State Film Awards.
dulquer-salmaan: Actor, producer and playback singer who works mainly in Malayalam and Telugu films, with occasional Tamil and Hindi roles; he is the son of Mammootty. His awards include five Filmfare Awards South and a Kerala State Film Award.
manoj-bajpai: Actor who has appeared in more than 70 films, mostly in Hindi, and is known for intense, layered performances. He has won four National Film Awards, and also leads the web series The Family Man.
rajkummar-rao: Hindi film actor who has worked across independent and mainstream cinema in more than thirty films, known for his range across genres. He won a National Film Award for Shahid, and his recent films include Bhool Chuk Maaf.
hansika-motwani: Actress who works mainly in Tamil and Telugu films. She started out as a child actor in Hindi films before moving to lead roles in Telugu with films such as Desamuduru and Kantri, and later became a familiar face in Tamil comedy-horror hits like Aranmanai 2.
mithun-chakraborty: Actor, producer, entrepreneur and politician whose five-decade career spans about 350 films, mostly in Hindi and Bengali. The disco-era star has kept working steadily, with recent roles in The Bengal Files and Jailer 2.
nani: Telugu actor and producer, often called Natural Star, and one of the most popular and highest-paid names in Telugu cinema. He has won two Nandi Awards and several Filmfare Awards, and his recent films include Hi Nanna and The Paradise.
anu-malik: Composer, singer and arranger who has written music mainly for Hindi films since the 1980s; he is the son of composer Sardar Malik. He has won a National Film Award and three Filmfare Awards.
sushmita-sen: Actress and former Miss Universe (1994), the first Indian woman to win the title. She has worked mainly in Hindi films and won a Filmfare Award, and returned to the spotlight with the web series Aarya.
dia-mirza: Actress and producer who works mostly in Hindi films. She was crowned Miss Asia Pacific International in 2000 before starting her film career, and her recent work includes Dhak Dhak and the Telugu film Wild Dog.
jimmy-shergill: Actor and producer who works in Hindi and Punjabi films, known for dependable supporting and lead roles in both. His recent Hindi films include Auron Mein Kahan Dum Tha.
ashish-vidyarthi: Actor known for villains and character roles across Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Bengali, Kannada, Malayalam and other languages. He won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor for Drohkaal in 1995.
nedumudi-venu: Actor and screenwriter from Kerala (1944–2021) who appeared in more than 500 films, mostly Malayalam and some Tamil, over nearly five decades. He also wrote screenplays and directed, and was one of Malayalam cinema's most respected character actors.
ram-charan: Telugu actor, producer and entrepreneur, son of Chiranjeevi, known for his dancing and for RRR, which brought him a worldwide audience. One of the highest-paid actors in Telugu cinema, he has been on Forbes India's Celebrity 100 list.
devi-sri-prasad: Composer, singer and lyricist known mainly for Telugu films, along with Tamil and Hindi work; fans call him DSP. His honours include a National Film Award, a Nandi Award and eleven Filmfare Awards.
kiara-advani: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films and is one of the country's highest-paid actresses. She has won an IIFA Award, and her recent films include Game Changer and Toxic.
pooja-hegde: Actress working in Telugu, Hindi and Tamil films and one of the highest-paid actresses in South Indian cinema. She has won four SIIMA Awards.
ravi-mohan: Tamil actor, formerly known as Jayam Ravi, the son of film editor A. Mohan and younger brother of director Mohan Raja. He made his lead debut in his brother's Jayam, whose success gave him his early screen name.
tusshar-kapoor: Actor and producer who works in Hindi films, best known for comedy franchises such as Golmaal; he is the son of actor Jeetendra and brother of producer Ekta Kapoor.
priyamani: Actress who works in Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Malayalam and Hindi films. She won the National Film Award for Best Actress, along with three Filmfare Awards South, and is also known for the web series The Family Man.
keerthy-suresh: Actress working mainly in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam films. She won the National Film Award for Best Actress for playing Savitri in Mahanati, and has also won Filmfare Awards South and SIIMA Awards.
anushka-sharma: Actress and producer who works in Hindi films and was one of the leading stars of the 2010s. She has won a Filmfare Award and three IIFA Awards, and her films include Sanju and Sui Dhaaga.
divya-dutta: Actress who works mainly in Hindi and Punjabi cinema, known for strong supporting roles. She has won a National Film Award and a Filmfare OTT Award.
pawan-kalyan: Telugu star turned politician who became Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 2024; he is the younger brother of Chiranjeevi and a trained martial artist. His recent films include Hari Hara Veera Mallu.
rajpal-yadav: Actor and comedian working mainly in Hindi cinema. His breakthrough came with a negative role in Ram Gopal Varma's Jungle, but he became best known for slapstick comedy, including the Bhool Bhulaiyaa films.
sonu-sood: Actor, producer and humanitarian who works mainly in Hindi, Telugu and Tamil films and is best known on screen for villain roles. He drew nationwide praise for helping stranded migrant workers during the 2020 lockdown.
siddharth: Actor who works in Tamil, Telugu and Hindi films, and has also written, produced and sung for films. His recent work includes Ayalaan and Test.
yuvan-shankar-raja: Composer and playback singer who scores mainly Tamil films, with some Telugu, Kannada and Hindi work; he is the son of Ilaiyaraaja. He is known for his versatility and for popular background scores, including Mankatha.
mani-sharma: Composer and music producer known mainly for Telugu films, with work in Tamil and Kannada as well. He was one of the busiest Telugu music directors of the late 1990s and 2000s, especially for big star vehicles.
nandamuri-balakrishna: Telugu actor, producer and politician, the son of matinee idol and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. T. Rama Rao. Known to fans as Balayya, he remains a mass hero, with recent hits including Veera Simha Reddy and Bhagavanth Kesari.
genelia-d-souza: Actress who works in Hindi, Telugu and Tamil films and was one of the leading South Indian heroines of the 2000s. She has won a Filmfare Award South, and also produces films.
mamta-mohandas: Actress, producer and playback singer who works mainly in Malayalam, Tamil and Telugu films. She has won a Kerala State Film Award and two Filmfare Awards South, and appeared in Maharaja.
chandra-mohan: Veteran Telugu actor (died 2023) whose career ran from the 1960s into the 2020s, first in lead roles and later as a much-loved character actor. His last films include DJ: Duvvada Jagannadham and Most Eligible Bachelor.
nivin-pauly: Actor and producer working mainly in Malayalam films, popular since Premam. He has won two Kerala State Film Awards and three Filmfare Awards South.
aditya-chopra: Director, producer and studio head who runs Yash Raj Films, the company founded by his father Yash Chopra. He directed Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge and has produced many of Hindi cinema's biggest hits, including Pathaan.
bhavana: Actress who works mainly in Malayalam films, with Tamil and Kannada roles too. She made her debut at 15 in the Malayalam film Nammal.
dino-morea: Actor and former supermodel, one of the best-known faces of Indian fashion in the late 1990s before he moved into films. He has acted mainly in Hindi, with some Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam and Telugu roles, and also produces.
kriti-sanon: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films, with a start in Telugu. She won the National Film Award for Best Actress for Mimi and has also won two Filmfare Awards; her recent films include Tere Ishk Mein.
karan-johar: Producer, director and television host who heads Dharma Productions and has launched the careers of many actors and filmmakers. He directed films such as Kuch Kuch Hota Hai and Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani, and hosts Koffee with Karan.
meera-jasmine: Actress who works in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada films. She debuted in 2001 in Lohithadas's Soothradharan and won the National Film Award for Best Actress for Paadam Onnu: Oru Vilapam.
yami-gautam: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films, with early roles in Telugu and Tamil. Her honours include a National Film Award, and her recent films include Article 370.
arya: Actor and producer who works mostly in Tamil films, with a few Malayalam and Telugu roles. He has won two Filmfare Awards South and two Tamil Nadu State Film Awards, and is known for Madrasapattinam and Sarpatta Parambarai.
jayaram: Actor who works mainly in Malayalam films, with Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Hindi roles too, and more than 200 films to his name. He is also a chenda percussionist, mimicry artist and occasional singer, and is known for family comedies.
jagathy-sreekumar: Malayalam actor, director and playback singer with well over a thousand films, widely regarded as one of the greatest comic actors in Malayalam cinema. A road accident in 2012 interrupted his career, and he returned to the screen in CBI 5: The Brain.
ronnie-screwvala: Entrepreneur, investor and film producer who founded UTV and later RSVP Movies. His productions range from Rang De Basanti to recent films such as Azaad.
marthand-k-venkatesh: Film editor who works in Telugu cinema and has won four Nandi Awards for his work.
ayesha-takia: Former actress who worked mainly in Hindi films. After ads and music videos, she debuted in Taarzan: The Wonder Car and became known for films such as Wanted and Paathshaala.
tanikella-bharani: Actor, screenwriter, poet and playwright who works mainly in Telugu cinema. He has acted in more than 750 films, a few in Tamil, Kannada and Hindi, and has written screenplays for 52 films.
ali: Telugu actor, comedian and television presenter who has appeared in more than a thousand Telugu films since starting as a child actor. He has won two Nandi Awards and two Filmfare Awards South.
neha-dhupia: Actress, model and Femina Miss India 2002, who represented India at Miss Universe that year. She works mainly in Hindi films and on television, with recent roles in Hindi Medium and Single Papa.
parvathy-thiruvothu: Actress who works mainly in Malayalam and Tamil films and is known for bold, performance-led roles. Her honours include a National Film Award, two Kerala State Film Awards and six Filmfare Awards.
sathyaraj: Tamil actor, producer and media personality with more than 260 films, also working in Telugu, Hindi, Malayalam and Kannada. He moved from villains to heroes to character roles, and reached a national audience as Kattappa in the Baahubali films.
mrunal-thakur: Actress who works mainly in Hindi and Telugu films after starting on television. She has won a Filmfare Award South and three SIIMA Awards, and is known for Sita Ramam and Super 30.
sidharth-malhotra: Actor who works in Hindi films, debuting in Student of the Year and winning wide praise for playing Captain Vikram Batra in Shershaah. He has appeared on Forbes India's Celebrity 100 list.
sidhique: Malayalam actor and producer who has worked in Malayalam cinema since the 1980s, moving between comic, character and villain roles. He appears in the Drishyam films as a key supporting character.
parineeti-chopra: Actress who works in Hindi films and won a National Film Award (Special Mention) and a Filmfare Award for her debut, Ishaqzaade. Her recent films include Mission Raniganj and Amar Singh Chamkila.
aftab-shivdasani: Actor, producer and model who works mainly in Hindi films, starting as a child actor after being picked as the Farex baby as an infant. He is best known for the Masti comedy series.
amrita-rao: Actress known for girl-next-door roles in Hindi films such as Main Hoon Na and Vivah. She has won an IIFA Award, and returned in Jolly LLB 3.
farhan-akhtar: Actor, director, writer and singer, the son of writers Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani, who co-founded Excel Entertainment in 1999. He directed Dil Chahta Hai and Don, and starred in Bhaag Milkha Bhaag.
naga-chaitanya: Telugu actor and entrepreneur, son of Nagarjuna. He has won a Filmfare Award South and a Nandi Award, and his recent films include Thandel.
sukumari: Actress (1940–2013) who appeared in more than 2,500 films over five decades, mostly in Malayalam and Tamil with some Telugu and Hindi. She won a National Film Award and was honoured with the Padma Shri.
urmila-matondkar: Actress turned politician known mainly for Hindi films such as Rangeela and Satya, with roles in Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi and Tamil cinema too. She began as a child actor in Masoom.
s-thaman: Composer and playback singer working mainly in Telugu and Tamil cinema. He won the National Film Award for Best Music Direction for Ala Vaikunthapurramuloo.
sharman-joshi: Actor who works in Hindi films and is best remembered as Raju in 3 Idiots. He has won an IIFA Award.
fardeen-khan: Actor who works mainly in Hindi films, the son of actor-producer Feroz Khan. He won a Filmfare Award for his debut, Prem Aggan, and returned to the screen after a long break with Heeramandi and Raja Shivaji.
johnny-lever: Actor and comedian who rose from stand-up and mimicry to become one of the best-known comic faces of Hindi cinema. He has appeared in hundreds of films, most memorably in the comedies of the 1990s and 2000s.
konkona-sen-sharma: Actress and filmmaker who works in Hindi and Bengali films, the daughter of filmmaker Aparna Sen. She has won two National Film Awards and three Filmfare Awards, and directed A Death in the Gunj.
salim-kumar: Malayalam actor, director and writer (1969–2026) who appeared in more than 300 films and was one of the most loved comic actors in Malayalam cinema. He won the National Film Award for Best Actor for Adaminte Makan Abu.
tiger-shroff: Hindi film actor and singer, the son of Jackie Shroff and Ayesha Dutt, known for action films and dance. He debuted in Heropanti and leads the Baaghi series.
ilaiyaraaja: Composer, conductor, arranger and singer who has scored more than a thousand films, mostly Tamil but also Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada and Hindi. Called Isaignani by fans, he is one of the most prolific and influential film composers in the world.
mahesh-manjrekar: Actor, director, writer and producer who works in Hindi, Marathi and Telugu films. He is best known for directing Vaastav, Astitva and Viruddh, and for playing gruff character roles.
radhika-apte: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films and streaming shows, along with Bengali, Marathi, Tamil and Telugu work. She came from theatre and became known for independent films and series such as Sacred Games.
rana-daggubati: Telugu actor, producer and entrepreneur who also works in Tamil and Hindi, best known as Bhallaladeva in the Baahubali films. His honours include a National Film Award and three Filmfare Awards South.
ravi-kishan: Actor, producer and television personality known as a Bhojpuri cinema star, with roles in Hindi and Telugu films too. He has been the Member of Parliament for Gorakhpur since 2019.
vivek: Tamil actor and comedian (1961–2021), often called Chinna Kalaivanar, whose comedy carried social messages. He was also a television personality, singer and environmental activist, honoured with the Padma Shri.
abhay-deol: Hindi film actor from the Deol family, who debuted in Imtiaz Ali's Socha Na Tha. He is known for choosing offbeat and independent films such as Dev.D, Oye Lucky! Lucky Oye! and Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara.
amala-paul: Actress and producer who works mainly in Tamil and Malayalam films. She has won a Tamil Nadu State Film Award, a Filmfare Award South and two SIIMA Awards.
anand-raj-anand: Composer, lyricist and playback singer in Hindi films, whose breakthrough was the song Chhota Bachha Jaan Ke from Masoom (1996). He went on to score films such as Kaante, Musafir and Welcome.
kunchacko-boban: Malayalam actor and producer, affectionately called Chackochan, who was the romantic 'chocolate boy' of the early 2000s and later reinvented himself in thrillers and character-driven films.
sunny-leone: Canadian-American actress, model and media personality who has worked in Hindi films since the 2010s. She is known for lead roles in thrillers and for many popular dance numbers.
bhumi-pednekar: Hindi film actress known for playing headstrong small-town women, starting with her debut in Dum Laga Ke Haisha. She has won three Filmfare Awards.
imran-khan: Actor of Indian origin who worked in Hindi films, debuting in Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na; he is Aamir Khan's nephew. He won a Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut and returned in Happy Patel: Khatarnak Jasoos.
kotagiri-venkateswara-rao: Film editor who has worked mainly in Telugu cinema for decades, cutting films such as Vinaya Vidheya Rama and Sita Ramam.
vidyasagar: Composer, musician and singer who scores mainly Tamil, Malayalam and Telugu films. He debuted as a film composer with the Tamil film Poo Manam in 1989, after years as an assistant and conductor, and won a National Film Award for Swarabhishekam.
karthi: Tamil actor, son of veteran actor Sivakumar and younger brother of Suriya, who started as an assistant director on Aayutha Ezhuthu. He debuted in Paruthiveeran and played Vandiyathevan in Ponniyin Selvan.
wamiqa-gabbi: Actress who works in Hindi and Punjabi films, with some Malayalam work. She first appeared as a child in Jab We Met and became a leading lady in Punjabi cinema before her Hindi roles.
arjun-sarja: Actor, producer and director who works mainly in Tamil films, with Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam and Hindi roles; the media call him Action King for his patriotic action films. His recent films include Mankatha.
biju-menon: Actor who works mainly in Malayalam films, with some Tamil, Telugu and Kannada roles, and more than 150 films since his 1995 debut in Puthran. He won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor for Ayyappanum Koshiyum.
jiiva: Tamil actor and producer, the youngest son of producer R. B. Choudary. He is known for Ko and Katradhu Thamizh, and played Krishnamachari Srikkanth in the Hindi film 83.
k-p-a-c-lalitha: Malayalam actress (1947–2022) who began in theatre with the KPAC troupe and acted in hundreds of films. She won two National Film Awards for Best Supporting Actress, and her later films include Bheeshma Parvam.
kalki-koechlin: French actress and writer who works mainly in Hindi films and on stage, known for an unconventional body of work beginning with Dev.D. She has won a National Film Award, for Margarita with a Straw.
kay-kay-menon: Actor who works mainly in Hindi cinema, with some Gujarati, Tamil, Marathi and Telugu roles. He is best known for Black Friday, Sarkar, Gulaal, Haider and The Ghazi Attack, and for series such as Farzi.
m-m-keeravani: Composer, singer and lyricist known mainly for Telugu cinema, credited as M. M. Kreem in Hindi films. He won the Academy Award and Golden Globe for the song Naatu Naatu from RRR, and also scored the Baahubali films.
silambarasan-tr: Tamil actor, filmmaker and musician, known as STR and the son of filmmaker T. Rajendar, who started as a child actor. His recent films include Thug Life.
sonali-bendre: Actress known mainly for Hindi and Telugu films and one of the leading heroines of the 1990s, in films such as Sarfarosh. She has won two Filmfare Awards.
vijay-deverakonda: Telugu actor and producer who broke through with Pelli Choopulu and Arjun Reddy and became one of the most popular young stars in Telugu cinema. He has won a Filmfare Award and a Nandi Award.
vishal-shekhar: Composer duo of Vishal Dadlani and Shekhar Ravjiani, known mainly for Hindi film music and also for Telugu, Tamil and Marathi work. Their soundtracks include Om Shanti Om, Chennai Express and Pathaan.
arjun-kapoor: Hindi film actor, the son of producer Boney Kapoor and Mona Shourie Kapoor, who debuted in Ishaqzaade. His recent films include Ek Villain Returns and Singham Again.
shankar-ehsaan-loy: Composer trio of Shankar Mahadevan, Ehsaan Noorani and Loy Mendonsa, with more than 50 soundtracks across Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam, Telugu, Marathi and English. Their work runs from Dil Chahta Hai to Gully Boy and Sam Bahadur.
v-t-vijayan: Film editor who works in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam cinema, with credits such as Boologam and Saamy Square.
vishal: Tamil actor and producer who runs Vishal Film Factory and is known for action films. He received the Kalaimamani award in 2006, and his recent films include Mark Antony.
ram-pothineni: Telugu actor known for energetic action and romantic films, including iSmart Shankar and its sequel Double iSmart. He has won a Filmfare Award and a SIIMA Award.
sayaji-shinde: Marathi actor known across Telugu, Tamil, Hindi and Marathi cinema, often as a villain or authority figure. He made his name in Hindi with Shool and has since appeared in a long list of South Indian films.
diljit-dosanjh: Singer, actor and producer who works in Punjabi music and in Punjabi and Hindi films. Several of his films, including the Jatt & Juliet series, are among the highest-grossing Punjabi films ever, and his Hindi work includes Amar Singh Chamkila.
sanjay-mishra: Actor known for Hindi films and television, who moved from comic roles to acclaimed lead performances. He has twice won the Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actor, for Ankhon Dekhi and Vadh.
amrish-puri: Actor (1932–2005) and one of the most notable figures in Hindi cinema and theatre, remembered for towering villains such as Mogambo in Mr. India and for warm character roles later in his career.
bhushan-kumar: Film and music producer who chairs T-Series (Super Cassettes Industries), one of India's biggest music labels and film studios. His recent productions include Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3.
soha-ali-khan: Actress who has worked in Hindi, Bengali and English films, the daughter of Sharmila Tagore and cricketer Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi and sister of Saif Ali Khan. She is known for Rang De Basanti.
adil-hussain: Actor from Assam known for work in independent and mainstream films in India and abroad, including Life of Pi. He received National Film Awards for Hotel Salvation and the Assamese film Maj Rati Keteki.
arbaaz-khan: Actor and producer who works mainly in Hindi films, with some Telugu and Malayalam roles; he is the brother of Salman Khan. He produced the Dabangg films and directed Dabangg 2.
celina-jaitly: Former actress who worked mainly in Hindi films after winning Femina Miss India 2001 and placing fourth runner-up at Miss Universe that year.
mallika-sherawat: Actress who works mainly in Hindi films and became widely known for bold roles in Khwahish and Murder.
nushrratt-bharuccha: Hindi film actress who started on television and gained recognition with Love Sex Aur Dhokha and the Pyaar Ka Punchnama films. Her later films include Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar.
regina-cassandra: Actress who works mainly in Telugu, Tamil and Hindi films. She has won a SIIMA Award, and her recent work includes Jaat.
sajid-wajid: Composer duo of brothers Sajid Khan and Wajid Khan, known for Hindi film music, especially the Dabangg films and many Salman Khan soundtracks. Wajid Khan died in June 2020.
indukuri-sunil-varma: Telugu actor known simply as Sunil, with more than 180 films, mostly comic roles, before he also played leads and villains. He has won three Nandi Awards and two Filmfare Awards South.
kartik-aaryan: Hindi film actor who broke through with Pyaar Ka Punchnama and later led hits such as Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2 and 3. He has won a National Film Award and a Filmfare Award, for Chandu Champion.
mahima-chaudhry: Actress who works in Hindi films, debuting in the 1997 romance Pardes. She returned to the screen in Emergency.
neena-gupta: Actress and television director who has worked in Hindi films and series for decades. She has won three National Film Awards and a Filmfare Award, and had a late-career resurgence with Badhaai Ho and Panchayat.
vadivelu: Tamil actor, comedian and occasional playback singer, one of the best-loved comedians in Tamil cinema, with around 290 credits. He has won two Filmfare Awards South and six Tamil Nadu State Film Awards.
anurag-kashyap: Director, writer, producer and actor known for gritty Hindi films such as Black Friday, Gangs of Wasseypur and Dev.D. He has won four Filmfare Awards, and also acts in Tamil and Telugu films such as Maharaja.
kavya-madhavan: Former actress who worked mainly in Malayalam films, with a few Tamil roles. She began as a child artist in 1991 and had her first lead role in Lal Jose's Chandranudikkunna Dikkil.
